answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost.
